motion.purpose: Discharge flare, arrival flare, disclosure chevron.

motion.purpose: Charge/discharge period, alive.

motion.name: period-busy
motion.purpose: Charge/discharge period, working.

motion.name: period-partial
motion.purpose: Charge/discharge period, partly down.

motion.name: period-failing
motion.purpose: Charge/discharge period, failing.

motion.name: charge
motion.value: linear over the period; stroke-opacity 0.18 -> 1 at 86%, 0.12 at 89%
motion.purpose: The ring filling with light, then letting go.

motion.name: discharge
motion.value: opacity 0 until 84%, peak at 88%, 0 at 100%; ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Halo and core flash as the ring discharges.

motion.name: crackle
motion.purpose: Filaments flickering while the part runs.

motion.name: pulse-run
motion.purpose: A spike running a fibre for a real hand-off.

motion.name: pulse-arrival
motion.purpose: The receiving node's one flare.

motion.name: signal-replay
motion.purpose: Recent signals replayed on opening.

motion.name: twinkle
motion.purpose: 34 twinkling stars.

motion.name: fail-ring
motion.purpose: Red ring pulse on a failing node.

motion.name: drift
motion.purpose: A node floating a few field units.

motion.name: view-move
motion.value: 420ms exponential ease-out, zoom in log space
motion.purpose: Pan, zoom and fit animations.

motion.name: disclosure
motion.purpose: Chevron turning 90° as details open.

motion.name: jump-in
motion.value: 900ms ease-in cubic to 22x the fitted zoom, node held on the camera path
motion.purpose: Flying into a node.

motion.name: warp
motion.value: 340 streaks (40% part-tinted) radiating from the node; ease-in cubic building, vanishing point eased to centre
motion.purpose: Stars streaking out during the jump (canvas).

motion.name: flood-in
motion.value: 900ms cubic-bezier(0.55, 0, 0.9, 0.4); hidden to 45%, 0.6 at 70%, full at 100%
motion.purpose: The part's light flooding the screen.

motion.name: flood-held
motion.purpose: The light settling under the open page.

motion.name: page-in
motion.purpose: A part page appearing.

motion.name: jump-out
motion.value: 800ms ease-out cubic; flood shrinks, streaks fall back, camera returns to the saved view
motion.purpose: Esc, back or the back link.

motion.name: overlay-fade
motion.purpose: Top-left text fades as a jump begins; bottom chrome and map nodes fade while a page is open.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Charge, discharge, crackle, twinkle, drift and the fail pulse stop; pulses land as a bare arrival; view changes and the jump happen instantly (flood and page-in run 1ms).

narrative.overview:
Jophiel's parts are electric neurons hanging in a night sky. Each part is a charged node: a white-hot core in its own color, a thin ring around it that fills with light over the part's beat and then discharges in one flare, and fine jagged filaments that crackle while it's alive. Between the nodes run conducting fibres, hairlines inside a faint glow that blend from one part's color to the other's. When one part really hands work to another, a spike of light runs the fibre and the core it reaches flares. Behind everything is a still star field at infinity, about a third of it tinted with the parts' own colors so the sky belongs to the same system. Everything the visitor reads on the field besides the nodes is quiet instrument overlay: a specimen label with live counts and the last signal top left, a magnification readout on a tick ruler bottom left, round zoom controls bottom right. The world refuses the category default for "system status": no node-graph dashboard of rounded boxes, neon edges and a stats sidebar.

The field is full-bleed and spatial, not paged. It is a map you drag, wheel, pinch and key around, from ×1 (the whole field) to ×6; past ×1.9 each node's sub-cores resolve inside its ring, fully legible by ×2.7, while the core shrinks to make room. Clicking a node is a jump, not a panel: the stars streak out from the node like a jump to lightspeed, the camera flies in with the node held on its path, the node's light floods the screen, and the part opens as its own page at `/system/:part`. The page sits over the field it was jumped into, the stars still faintly there: a sticky left rail with the live node, its name, state, role, sub-parts, workers and hand-offs, beside a readable timeline of the part's real recent records. Esc, the back button or "← System" plays the jump in reverse. The density is low on the field and comfortable, editorial-readable, on the part page.

**Scope.** This world is built only on the owner-only System page (`/system`) and its part pages (`/system/:part`). The rest of the app (chat, voice dashboard, login, integrations, predict) predates it, uses a light pale-blue and lavender look written as hardcoded Tailwind hexes, and is an **unrecorded incumbent**: this file records no tokens for it, and nothing here should be read as describing it. The older dark `@theme` block at the top of `frontend/src/index.css` (Space Grotesk, teal accent) is not this world either; the System page does not use it.

**History and divergences.** The first build was a fluorescence-microscope look; the electric-neuron world replaced it so pulses read as current. This refresh replaces the right-hand details sheet (and its bottom-sheet form on phones) with the jump into a part page. The part colors, type, chrome and node anatomy carried over. There is still no physical scale bar: magnification is a tick ruler marked at ×1, ×2, ×4 and ×6, because a µm unit would be a made-up claim. The direction contract says fibres thicken with zoom along with filaments and rings; the build thickens only filaments and rings, and fibres stay a fixed 1.1px hairline. The build is recorded here.
keyCharacteristics: Night field (#040506) of star points, about a third tinted in part colors, a few twinkling, fixed at infinity and moving at half the pan.
One color per part, kept everywhere that part appears, on the field and on its page.
Nodes as charge: white-hot core, charging ring, crackling jagged filaments, discharge flare on the state's beat.
Fibres as conductors: a 1.1px line in a 6px glow, sender-to-receiver gradient; real hand-offs run them as tapered spikes.
A node opens by a jump: streaking stars, a fly-in, the part's light flooding the screen, then its own page; back plays it in reverse.
Part pages are a sticky rail plus a rule-divided timeline with a time column, never cards.
Overlay chrome in Schibsted Grotesk with tabular figures; round glass zoom buttons.
Reduced motion gets a still field and a jump without animation.

rules.name: The One Color Rule
rules.body: A part has exactly one color, and that color appears wherever the part does: core, ring, filaments, fibre ends, pulse tail, sub-cores, the flood of the jump, and on its page the glyph, state word, sub-part dots, meta lines, reasoning rule and focus ring. A part is never given a second hue, and a part color is never borrowed for anything that isn't its part. The shared uses are Cognition cyan as the map's default focus ring, and the tinted stars, which only ever carry the seven part colors.

rules.name: The Red Means Failing Rule
rules.body: Fail Red (#FF4136) is reserved for a failing part: its ring and its state word, on the field and on its page. Error prose (a failed record, a worker error, a load failure) uses the softer Error Text (#FF8A80). No other surface uses red.

rules.name: The Light Is State Rule
rules.body: State is told by charge, not badges: the ring charges and discharges on the state's period (alive 2.8 s, working 1.05 s, partly down 4.4 s, failing 1.6 s); the node dims to 72% when partly down, 45% unknown, 28% down and 14% off on the field (the page glyph uses 75%, 45%, 30% and 16%).

rules.name: The Sentence Case Rule
rules.body: All overlay and page text is sentence case and untracked (beyond the negative tracking on names and headings). No uppercase tracked labels.

rules.name: The Tabular Figures Rule
rules.body: Any number that updates live (counts, magnification, "1 s", "46 s", "7 min") is set in tabular figures so it doesn't jitter.

rules.name: The Stars At Infinity Rule
rules.body: The sky never scales with the zoom and never carries meaning; only nodes, fibres and pulses are signal. Star tints are the parts' colors for belonging, not for state. Nothing sits on a card above the field; a part page replaces the view rather than floating over it.

dos: Do give every part its one color and carry it to its ring, filaments, fibres, pulse tails, sub-cores, its jump and its page (The One Color Rule).
Do show state as charge: the ring's beat, the discharge flare, dimming, a broken ring, a red ring.
Do keep the field full-bleed on Field Black (#040506) with the star field at infinity behind the nodes.
Do run a pulse only for a real hand-off between two parts.
Do set live numbers in tabular figures and ring field labels in Field Black.
Do open a part by jumping into it and close it by playing the jump in reverse; give each part page its own address.
Do show a part's records as a timeline: a time column, a part-color meta line, rule-divided entries.
Do link a sub-part in the rail only when it has a section on the page.

Do stop charging, discharge, crackle, twinkle, drift and the failing pulse under `prefers-reduced-motion`, let pulses land as a bare arrival, and jump view changes and dives instead of animating them.
donts: Don't draw parts as rounded boxes, neon edges or a stats sidebar: the node-graph dashboard is the default this world refuses.
Don't put records in rounded cards on this page; part pages are rule-divided timelines.
Don't bring back a side sheet or modal card for a part; the jump and its page replace it.
Don't add a physical scale bar or µm units; magnification is the ×1–×6 tick ruler.
Don't use red for anything but failure.
Don't let the stars scale with the zoom or carry state, or tint them with anything but the part colors.
Don't set uppercase, letter-spaced labels on the field or pages (The Sentence Case Rule).
Don't extend these tokens to the rest of the app; the light incumbent there is a separate, unrecorded look.
